about: Curated input of scripts/licenses.py: the environments to read, licence corrections for packages whose metadata are missing or contradicted, and the tools, data sources and services. Every entry lists the pages or files opened to confirm it, with the date. status is 'confirmed' when the licence or terms were read at those sources, 'not confirmed' otherwise (the entry then says what was found).

environments.purpose: Main pipeline (`bsc` stages, tests, page build)
DENSS envelopes (`bsc envelopes` runs `denss-all` from here)

direct.source: the install line in README.md, section The DENSS environment (`pip install "numpy<2" denss`)

environments.purpose: BioEmu package for the bioemu-v1.2 re-sample analysis (local conversion of the sampled batches; sampling itself ran on Colab)

direct.source: the install cell of `notebooks/bioemu_resample.ipynb` (`pip install "bioemu[cuda]" pandas`; the local environment has the CPU build)

environments.purpose: Playwright, used only to take screenshots of the project page while checking it; not part of the pipeline

direct.source: the environment's purpose (one package installed by hand)

bioemu.note: The wheel's metadata carry no License field or classifier; the LICENSE file of the repository is MIT.

namex.note: No licence in the metadata; the LICENSE file shipped in the wheel and the one in the repository are Apache 2.0.

openmm.licence: MIT (API, Reference and CPU platforms) AND LGPL (CUDA and OpenCL platforms)
openmm.note: The metadata say 'Python Software Foundation License (BSD-like)'; OpenMM's Licenses.txt gives MIT for the API, Reference and CPU platforms and the LGPL for the CUDA and OpenCL platforms. The installed wheel ships the OpenCL plugin libraries; the simulations used the CPU platform.

mmtf-python.note: The License field says Apache 2.0 and the classifier says MIT; the repository's LICENSE.txt is Apache 2.0.

scipy.note: Metadata give the licence text and the BSD classifier without the variant; the repository's LICENSE.txt is BSD 3-Clause.

mrcfile.note: Metadata say 'BSD'; the repository's LICENSE.txt is BSD 3-Clause.

jinja2.note: Metadata carry only the BSD classifier; the repository's LICENSE.txt is BSD 3-Clause.

numba.note: Metadata say 'BSD'; the repository's LICENSE is BSD 2-Clause.

numpy.note: Version 1.26.4 (DENSS environment) gives the licence text and the BSD classifier; LICENSE.txt at v1.26.4 is BSD 3-Clause. Later versions carry a License-Expression and need no correction.

matplotlib.note: Metadata give the PSF classifier; the licence is the Matplotlib License Agreement, modelled on the PSF licence, which has no SPDX identifier.

tools.name: Pepsi-SAXS
tools.use: Computes the SAXS curve of each simulated conformer (`analysis/simulations/06_saxs.py`). The PeptoneBench authors used it to compute the archive's curves.
tools.obtained: Downloaded at run time by `analysis/simulations/02_fetch_sources.py` from the authors' server into `SIM_WORK` (git-ignored); sha256 in `results/simulations/sources.json`
tools.licence: Proprietary. Web page: "All rights reserved. The academic version is free." Program banner: "For academic use only!"
tools.restrictions: Academic use only. The page publishes no terms for other use.
tools.attribution: Cite Grudinin, Garkavenko & Kazennov, Acta Cryst. D73 (2017) 449-464

sources.what: banner printed by the downloaded binary (--help)

tools.name: PULCHRA
tools.use: Rebuilds all-atom models from the CALVADOS Cα frames before Pepsi-SAXS (`06_saxs.py`)
tools.obtained: C source downloaded at run time from KULL-Centre/papers at a pinned commit and compiled with gcc into `SIM_WORK` (git-ignored)
tools.licence: MIT (LICENSE file in pulchra_306.tgz, Copyright (c) 2000-2009 Piotr Rotkiewicz)
tools.restrictions: None beyond keeping the notice in copies
tools.attribution: Keep the MIT notice in copies; cite Rotkiewicz & Skolnick, J Comput Chem 2008

tools.name: MMseqs2
tools.use: Sequence searches of the constructs against the training sets and CATH S100 (`analysis/coverage/14_annotate_training.py`, `15_nearest_training.py`)
tools.obtained: Downloaded by hand from the GitHub release into `COVERAGE_WORK/tools` (command in `analysis/coverage/README.md`)
tools.licence: MIT (LICENSE.md at tag 18-8cc5c)

tools.name: DENSS
tools.use: Ab initio envelopes of the three worked examples; `bsc envelopes` runs the `denss-all` program as a separate process
tools.obtained: Python package in its own environment (`/scratch/.venv-denss`); maps written to `results/denss/` (git-ignored)
tools.redistributed: No; only fit statistics (`results/denss_stats.json`) and the figure drawn from the maps are tracked
tools.licence: GPL-3.0 (package metadata 'GPLv3'; repository LICENSE is GPL version 3)
tools.restrictions: Copyleft applies to anyone who distributes DENSS or a work based on it; the repo calls it as a program and ships none of it

tools.name: CALVADOS (code)
tools.use: Coarse-grained simulations; imported by `analysis/simulations/05_run.py`
tools.obtained: Installed into the simulation environment from GitHub at the pinned commit (`analysis/simulations/requirements.txt`)
tools.licence: GPL-3.0 (LICENSE at the pinned commit; package metadata GPL-3.0-only)
tools.restrictions: Copyleft applies to anyone who distributes CALVADOS or a work based on it. The repo's scripts import it but ship none of its code
tools.attribution: Cite Tesei et al. PNAS 2021; Tesei & Lindorff-Larsen, Open Res Europe 2022; Cao et al. Protein Sci 2024

tools.name: CALVADOS 3 residue parameters
tools.use: Force-field parameters of the simulations; `07_analyse.py` reads the residue masses from it
tools.obtained: Downloaded at run time by `02_fetch_sources.py` into `SIM_WORK` (git-ignored); sha256 in `results/simulations/sources.json`
tools.licence: GPL-3.0 (the file is part of the CALVADOS repository, whose LICENSE covers it; no separate licence for the parameters was found)
tools.attribution: Cite Cao et al. Protein Sci 2024

sources.what: KULL-Centre/CALVADOS repository at 6981542 (LICENSE at the root, no other licence file)

tools.name: OpenMM
tools.use: Simulation engine under CALVADOS
tools.obtained: Python package in the simulation environment
tools.licence: MIT for the API, Reference and CPU platforms; LGPL for the CUDA and OpenCL platforms (the wheel ships the OpenCL plugins)
tools.restrictions: None for use; LGPL terms bind redistribution of the CUDA and OpenCL platforms
tools.attribution: Cite Eastman et al. J Phys Chem B 2024 (OpenMM 8)

tools.name: metapredict
tools.use: Predicted disorder of the constructs, training sequences and CATH S35 sequences (`14_annotate_training.py`)
tools.obtained: Python package in the coverage environment; its network weights ship inside the package
tools.licence: MIT (package metadata and repository LICENSE)
tools.attribution: Cite Emenecker et al. Biophys J 2021

tools.name: BioEmu (code)
tools.version: archive ensembles: commit ac7455d (by the PeptoneBench authors); Colab re-sample: unpinned `bioemu[cuda]`; local: 1.4.1
tools.use: The model under study. The archive's ensembles were generated by the PeptoneBench authors; the notebook re-samples with bioemu-v1.2 on Colab; the local environment converts the sampled batches
tools.obtained: Python package (Colab and `/scratch/.venv-bioemu`)
tools.licence: MIT. The package bundles code derived from ColabFold (MIT), a patched subset of AlphaFold2 (Apache-2.0) and OpenFold code (Apache-2.0), as listed in its README

tools.name: BioEmu checkpoints
tools.use: Model weights; the notebook samples with bioemu-v1.2. The archive does not record which checkpoint it used
tools.obtained: Downloaded at run time from Hugging Face by `bioemu.sample`
tools.licence: MIT. The Hugging Face model repository, which holds all three checkpoints, declares `license: mit` and its card states 'License: MIT License'; no separate terms for any checkpoint were found

sources.what: Hugging Face API record (cardData.license, file list)

tools.name: AlphaFold2 parameters
tools.use: BioEmu computes its sequence embeddings with AlphaFold2 and downloads these weights on first use
tools.obtained: Downloaded at run time by BioEmu (Colab) from storage.googleapis.com
tools.licence: CC-BY-4.0 for the AlphaFold parameters; Apache-2.0 for the AlphaFold code. The README's statement covers 'the AlphaFold parameters' without naming release files

tools.name: ColabFold MMseqs2 MSA server
tools.use: BioEmu sends each query sequence to this server for its MSA when sampling (Colab notebook)
tools.obtained: External service called at run time
tools.redistributed: No; the MSAs stay in the sampling output
tools.licence: No licence or terms of service for the server were found. ColabFold's README asks that queries from a local computer be serial from a single IP and not spread over several computers. ColabFold code is MIT
tools.restrictions: Usage limits only, as stated in the README
tools.attribution: Cite Mirdita et al. Nat Methods 2022

sources.what: ColabFold README, FAQ on the MSA server

tools.name: Google Colab
tools.use: Runs `notebooks/bioemu_resample.ipynb` on a free GPU; output written to the user's Google Drive
tools.obtained: External service; the notebook only
tools.licence: Google Terms of Service plus the Colab Additional Terms of Service (last modified 14 May 2024)
tools.restrictions: No sharing of accounts and no resale of access; resource limits as set by Google

tools.name: Kaggle notebooks
tools.use: The notebook also detects Kaggle and writes its output there; an alternative runtime only
tools.obtained: External service
tools.licence: Kaggle Terms of Use; the page renders with JavaScript and its text could not be read

tools.name: GitHub, GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages
tools.use: Repository hosting; CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`: actions/checkout, astral-sh/setup-uv, ruff, pytest); the project page served from `docs/`
tools.obtained: External service
tools.licence: GitHub Terms of Service (effective 27 April 2026) and the additional terms for Actions and Pages. The two actions are MIT
tools.restrictions: Actions only for developing and testing the project; Pages not for commercial hosting; Pages sites at most 1 GB, soft limit 100 GB per month bandwidth. A public repository grants other users a licence to view and fork it through GitHub

tools.use: Creates the environments and runs the pipeline and CI
tools.obtained: Installed by hand; in CI by astral-sh/setup-uv
tools.licence: Apache-2.0 OR MIT (the repository carries LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT)

tools.name: Playwright and Chromium

tools.name: PeptoneBench code
tools.use: Not installed or imported. The score conventions in `src/bsc/saxs.py` and the Pepsi-SAXS flag in `analysis/simulations/common.py` follow it
tools.obtained: Not obtained
tools.licence: Apache-2.0

data.name: PeptoneBench archive, Zenodo 17306061
data.use: The 439 SAXS profiles with sequences, pH and disorder scores (PeptoneDB-SAXS, curated from SASBDB), and the ensembles and Pepsi-SAXS curves of BioEmu-1 and six other models (AlphaFold2, ESMFold, Boltz-2, IDPFold, idpSAM, PepTron)
data.attribution: Invernizzi et al. 2025 (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.10.18.680935) and the Zenodo record; the profiles also carry SASBDB's attribution to their depositors
data.tracked: Derived results: scores, reweighting paths, radii of gyration, classes, figures. Also copied as columns: the construct sequences (`results/entries.csv`, `results/simulations/inputs.csv`, `notebooks/resample_list.csv`) and the SASBDB entry titles
data.raw_redistributed: No profiles, curves or ensembles. Construct sequences are copied as table columns, which CC-BY-4.0 permits with attribution

data.name: SASBDB data and REST API
data.use: Entry summaries of the 439 profiles: measurement conditions, molecular weight, Dmax, organisms, UniProt codes (`bsc fetch`, `analysis/coverage/01_fetch_sasbdb.py`, `18_sasbdb_metadata.py`)
data.licence: "The data and models deposited in SASBDB are free of all copyright restrictions and made fully and freely available for both non-commercial and commercial use." No terms specific to the REST API were found
data.attribution: "Users of the data should attribute the original authors." Each entry is identified by its SASBDB code and the page links every code to its record; cite Kikhney et al. Protein Sci 2020
data.tracked: `results/coverage/sasbdb_metadata.csv` (curve type, instrument, buffer, pH, concentration, organisms, molecule names, project titles and contributor names per entry) and entry titles in `results/candidates.csv` and `results/entries.csv`
data.raw_redistributed: No scattering profiles. Entry metadata are copied as tables, which the SASBDB statement permits with attribution

data.name: BioEmu MD training sets, Zenodo 15629740, 15641199, 15641184
data.version: CATH1 and CATH2; octapeptides; MegaSim (published June 2025)
data.use: Zip listings and the `topology.pdb` of each CATH and MegaSim wild-type system, read through HTTP range requests; no trajectories
data.attribution: None required for Results (section 3.1: no restriction or obligation on the use, modification or sharing of Results); whoever shares the Data must include the agreement text. Cite Lewis et al. Science 2025
data.tracked: Derived results only: nearest-training identifiers and identities (`results/coverage/training_nearest.csv`), counts and compositions (`training_summary.json`)

data.name: BioEmu AFDB cluster definitions
data.use: The 50,228 pre-training clusters and their 179,422 AFDB v4 members (`11_download_bioemu_training.py`)
data.licence: MIT (the repository LICENSE at that commit; the folder's README states no other licence). The members are AlphaFold DB entries (CC-BY-4.0)
data.tracked: Derived results only (cluster counts, compositions, nearest-member identifiers)

data.name: AlphaFold DB
data.use: Not downloaded. The BioEmu clusters are AFDB v4 entries identified by UniProt accession, and TED's domains are cut from AFDB models
data.licence: CC-BY-4.0 ("Data is available for academic and commercial use, under a CC-BY-4.0 license"); use of the site is subject to the EMBL-EBI Terms of Use
data.attribution: Cite Jumper et al. Nature 2021 (the AlphaFold methods paper, as the licence page asks)

data.name: MEGAscale, Zenodo 7992926
data.use: The curated stability table and its wild-type domains (one zip member read through HTTP range requests)
data.attribution: Cite Tsuboyama et al. Nature 2023 and the Zenodo record

data.name: CATH
data.version: v4.4.0 classification files; v4.3.0 S35 list (sensitivity check)
data.use: Superfamily classification, S35 clusters and S100 sequences (`00_download_cath.sh`, `08_compare.py`, `14_annotate_training.py`)
data.licence: CC-BY-4.0 for the data. The CATH wiki text itself is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
data.attribution: Attribute to I. Sillitoe, N. Dawson, T. Lewis, D. Lee, J. Lees, C. Orengo, based on work at cath.biochem.ucl.ac.uk
data.tracked: `results/coverage/cath_superfamily_rank.csv.gz` (superfamily identifiers, S35 cluster counts, rank and CATH superfamily names) and derived comparisons
data.raw_redistributed: No classification files. Superfamily names and cluster counts are copied as table columns, which CC-BY-4.0 permits with attribution

data.name: InterPro, Pfam and CATH-Gene3D (InterPro API)
data.licence: InterPro and Pfam data: CC0-1.0 ("All of the InterPro, Pfam, PRINTS and SFLD downloadable data ... CC0 1.0"). CATH-Gene3D is not named in that statement; CATH's own data are CC-BY-4.0
data.attribution: Cite InterPro and the member databases (requested by InterPro); EMBL-EBI expects attribution
data.tracked: Gene3D superfamily identifiers and Pfam accessions per construct (`results/coverage/per_protein_mapping.csv`, `results/arm1/relatedness.csv`)
data.status: confirmed (InterPro, Pfam); not confirmed (CATH-Gene3D as served by InterPro)

data.name: UniProtKB, Swiss-Prot, UniParc, ID mapping, peptide search, taxonomy
data.use: Mapping constructs to accessions, sequences of the AFDB cluster members and named MD proteins, the Swiss-Prot reference set, organism lineages
data.licence: CC-BY-4.0 for all copyrightable parts of the databases; no separate terms for the REST services were found
data.attribution: Cite UniProt as on its citation page
data.tracked: Accessions, isoforms, ranges, organism and lineage per construct (`results/coverage/per_protein_mapping.csv`) and derived comparisons
data.raw_redistributed: No flat files or sequences from UniProt

data.name: RCSB PDB: search API, data API, clusters-by-entity-30, FASTA
data.use: Sequence search for unmapped constructs, polymer-entity data, the 30% clusters with their representatives, and the FASTA of the twelve DESRES fast-folder PDB entries
data.licence: CC0-1.0 for PDB archive files and data from the RCSB PDB APIs
data.attribution: Encouraged, not required: the original authors of the structures

data.name: PDBe SIFTS (best_structures API)
data.licence: No SIFTS-specific licence was found. The EMBL-EBI Terms of Use place no restrictions beyond those of the original data owners and expect attribution
data.attribution: The SIFTS page asks users to cite Dana et al. NAR 2019 (or Velankar et al. NAR 2013)
data.tracked: Derived coverage per construct (`has_pdb_50` and coverage fractions in `results/coverage/per_protein_mapping.csv`)

data.name: TED (The Encyclopedia of Domains)
data.use: CATH labels of domains in the AFDB model of each accession (`04_fetch_annotations.py`)
data.licence: The TED data release on Zenodo (record 10848710) is CC-BY-4.0. The API site renders with JavaScript and no terms could be read from it
data.attribution: Cite Lau et al. Science 2024 and the Zenodo record
data.tracked: TED superfamily labels per construct (`ted_superfamilies` in `results/coverage/per_protein_mapping.csv`)

data.name: CALVADOS training and validation protein lists
data.use: The proteins the CALVADOS 1, 2 and 3 parameters were trained and validated on, for the circularity check (`02_fetch_sources.py`, `03_circularity.py`)
data.licence: CALVADOS 1 lists (papers/2021/CG-IDPs-Tesei-et-al): CC-BY-4.0, from the LICENSE file in that folder. CALVADOS 2 lists (papers/2022/CG-cutoffs-Tesei-et-al): no licence file in the folder or at the repository root; the folder's README links Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.6815067, whose current version (record 7437501, an archive of the folder) is CC-BY-4.0; I did not check that the archive holds the same two files. CALVADOS 3 lists (_2024_Cao_CALVADOSCOM): MIT, Copyright (c) 2024 Linderstrøm-Lang Centre for Protein Science, University of Copenhagen
data.attribution: CC-BY-4.0: cite Tesei et al. PNAS 2021 and Tesei & Lindorff-Larsen 2022. MIT: keep the copyright and permission notice with copies of the files. Cite Cao et al. Protein Sci 2024
data.tracked: `results/simulations/calvados_sets.csv`: set, role, file, protein name and sequence copied from the eight list files; `circularity.csv` derived
data.raw_redistributed: Yes, names and sequences. Permitted for the CC-BY-4.0 and MIT files with attribution (given here); for the CALVADOS 2 files it rests on the Zenodo deposit

data.name: Folding@home COVID-19 cryptic-pockets bucket
data.use: Only the object listing, to count the simulated systems of one of BioEmu's MD sets (`11_download_bioemu_training.py`)
data.licence: CC0 (AWS Open Data Registry entry for the Folding@home COVID-19 datasets)

data.name: DESRES fast-folder simulations
data.use: Cited only. No DESRES data are downloaded or used; the twelve proteins' sequences come from their PDB entries at RCSB (row above)
data.licence: Not reviewed, since nothing is obtained from DESRES

sources.what: the code that fetches the twelve PDB sequences
